items.description: Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Jim Cramer said Home Depot's latest earnings report strengthened his confidence in the retailer's long-term prospects. He pointed to improving demand and market-share gains as reasons to buy the dip, arguing that Home Depot is well-positioned to benefit from an eventual housing recovery. CNBC's Jim Cramer said that Home Depot's third-quarter earnings report strengthened his confidence in the retailer's long-term prospects, rendering the stock's pullback Tuesday a buying opportunity. "I told CNBC Investing Club members today that, if we weren't restricted in the name, I would be buying today's dip and adding more Home Depot shares for my Charitable Trust," the " Mad Money " host said. "This was a good quarter, and the negative response just seems to be based on a myopic view of what the company was implying about the current quarter with its updated guidance." Shares of the home improvement retailer fell 2% despite reporting better-than-expected quarterly earnings and revenue. Same-store sales climbed 2.2%, marking the retailer's strongest comps performance in four years. The sell-off appeared driven by updated full-year guidance that implied slightly weaker-than-expected fourth-quarter results. But Cramer cautioned against reading too much into the forecast, noting Home Depot's history of conservative guidance, particularly as it prepares for a leadership transition. The company announced Tuesday that veteran CFO Richard McPhail will succeed Ted Decker as CEO next week. Decker, who went on temporary medical leave in August, will continue to serve as chair of the board. Home Depot shares have struggled to gain traction in recent years, as elevated interest rates weighed on housing activity and home improvement spending. Higher mortgage rates have discouraged homeowners from moving, reducing demand for the renovation projects that often accompany home sales. Shares have shown signs of life since reaching a 52-week low on Oct. 1, rallying roughly 20%, as bond yields retreated and investors rotated into consumer stocks. Still, the stock remains down 1% for the year. But Cramer argued that Home Depot's latest results offer reasons to own the stock while waiting for a decline in interest rates to spark a meaningful inflection for the business. "I heard enough from management to stay invested now, and I feel even better about the long-term prospects of Home Depot after today's report," he said. On the earnings call, incoming CEO McPhail highlighted strength in the repair and remodeling businesses, while 13 of Home Depot's 16 product categories posted positive comparable sales and online sales continued growing at a double-digit pace. Cramer said those encouraging demand trends, along with market-share gains among professional contractors, suggest Home Depot is strengthening its business even before the housing market recovers. "For those with a long-term view, the important part is that the company is taking share," he said. "Whenever the broader housing market does return, Home Depot is positioned to be one of the companies that stands to benefit the most." TransUnion, a leader in global information and insights, released its 2027 Personal and Commercial Lines Annual Insurance Outlook on Tuesday, which focuses on what the insurance industry needs to stay profitable in a changing market. The report states that personal line underwriting has been strong throughout this year, but companies need to assess their strategies going forward as fewer people buy cars and homes , therefore reducing the pool of potential policyholders. According to the report, the share of renters who convert to homeownership was 3.9% in 2025, a sharp decline from 7.2% in 2009. This represents a shocking 46% decrease in the share of renters transitioning to homeownership in just 14 years. Combined with a 2025 report from the National Association of Realtors®, which stated that the median age of first-time buyers climbed from 33 to 40 in just five years, TransUnion concluded that the pool of potential policyholders is shrinking. The decrease in renters buying homes goes back to affordability and economic pressure, according to Ryan Thomson of The Assumable Guy . “Renters didn't stop wanting to own. Rates tripled and prices kept climbing, so the monthly number stopped working,” Thomson tells Realtor.com® . “In Colorado Springs, where I sell, 71% of households could afford a median-priced home in 2019. By 2023, it was 25.3%. So renters stay put. However, the increased risk of severe weather in these states means they’re not always as affordable as they seem. (Stock image) Thomas/Adobe Stock “People may be assuming the Sun Belt states are generally affordable, and that isn't always the case,” Walker adds. “Property values are increasing in Sun Belt states because of in-migration, which increases property taxes and insurance costs, and inflates housing costs.” For insurance companies, TransUnion recommends strategies like focusing on retaining and creating more value from current customer, winning policies from competition, and combining risk mitigating and marketing efforts when discussing migration. For the housing market, improving outlooks and rebuilding the renter-to-homeowner path comes down to affordability and opportunity. “We need to increase the supply of entry-level, affordable housing. This includes promoting the construction of new housing in high-demand, high-growth communities. The industry needs to offer new financing options and improve responsibility to help new homebuyers qualify to enter the housing market,” says Walker. “People aren’t giving up their dreams of homeownership. They’re postponing them because the housing market has changed and the financial requirements to homeownership are out of the reach of many. The markets that can provide jobs and affordable housing will thrive, and gain the most, from future homeowners.”

items.title: British Land Ups Guidance As AI Drives Restructure And Possible Job Losses
items.description: Courtesy of Oxford Properties British Land's Jo McNamara British Land has upgraded its full-year earnings guidance after delivering 12% like-for-like rental growth in the first half, as its new chief executive looks to use artificial intelligence and automation to reshape the business and reduce costs. The FTSE 100 landlord reported underlying profit of £166M for the six months to 30 September, up 7% year-on year, while underlying earnings per share increased 5% to 16.1p. The company raised its full-year underlying EPS guidance to 31p, representing 7% annual growth, from previous guidance of at least 30.5p. However, alongside the improved performance, British Land Chief Executive Jo McNamara signalled a significant change in how the 170-year-old property company operates, with technology and AI expected to play an increasingly important role. “We are already beginning to see how AI, automation and better use of data can change the way businesses operate, and I want British Land to lean into that opportunity,” McNamara said at the results. The company has begun an organisational restructure intended to create a leaner business with clearer accountability, targeting annualised savings of £5M to £7M from financial year 2028, with British Land consulting on potential job cuts across its approximately 600-strong workforce. “This is not simply about taking cost out of the business. It is about amplifying judgement, enhancing productivity and reducing lower-value activity, freeing our people to spend more of their time with customers, on our assets and on the activities that create the most value,” McNamara added. British Land's campuses division recorded 25% like-for-like net rental growth, while retail and London urban logistics grew 2% and, across the portfolio, occupancy stood at 96%. The company completed lettings covering 1.4M SF during the period, at rents 8% ahead of previous passing rents and 10% above estimated rental value. A further 1.1M SF was under offer at rents 12% above ERV, the company said. The company also completed £765M of capital transactions, including £247M of disposals at a net initial yield of 4.7%, broadly in line with book value, while a further £328M of disposals had been exchanged or were under offer. Its portfolio valuation increased 1.5% during the half to £10.47B, while its loan-to-value ratio edged up to 40%, from 39.2% at the end of March. items.title: Fitch affirms Finance of America’s CCC rating as key risks, leverage persist
items.description: Finance of America Companies’ long-term credit ratings remain deep in speculative-grade territory, even as the company reduces near-term risk and improves underlying profitability, according to a review published Monday by Fitch Ratings . Fitch this week affirmed the long-term issuer default ratings of Finance of America Companies and its subsidiaries, Finance of America Equity Capital LLC and Finance of America Funding LLC, with a CCC rating and a positive outlook. Fitch also affirmed Finance of America Funding’s senior secured debt rating at CCC- with a recovery rating of RR5. Fitch defines CCC ratings as having a very low margin for safety, with default considered a real possibility. But the ratings agency also explained that it maintains a positive outlook for Finance of America (FOA) due to its "established market position within the reverse mortgage sector," along with experience senior management and support from Brian Libman, who chairs its board of directors. The action is part of Fitch's periodic peer review of nine publicly rated nonbank mortgage companies. Like other lenders, FOA has been contending with volatile interest rates , high leverage and constrained liquidity as the broader mortgage market remains cyclical and capital intensive. Earlier this month, FOA reported a net loss of $110 million in the third quarter of 2026 as noncash fair value adjustments offset growth in its home equity lending business. The company reported funded loan volume of $748 million from July through September, up 24% from the same period in 2025, while its year-to-date volume of $2.07 billion was up 17% year over year. The company also said during its Q3 earnings call that it expects to complete a $60 million paydown of senior secured notes in November. In June 2024, FOA announced a restructuring of unsecured debt into secure notes while extending the original 2025 maturity date. That debt was restructured into two tranches, with $200 million in secured first-lien notes due in 2026 (along with an option to extend to 2027) and $150 million in exchangeable senior first-lien notes due in 2029. Why FOA's rating was affirmed In its report , Fitch said the positive outlook reflects FOA’s work over the past year to address material near-term obligations and its improved profitability when excluding fair value marks. The agency indicated it could raise FOA’s issuer default rating to B- if the company builds a “substantial” liquidity cushion beyond remaining repayment obligations and continues to de-lever through retained earnings. The ratings remain constrained by relatively weak liquidity and high leverage, a short-term and largely secured funding profile, and elevated key person risk tied to Libman. Additionally, the review factored in the highly cyclical nature of mortgage originations, as well as the volatility tied to mortgage servicing rights valuations and securitization residuals. The announcement illustrates that while FOA has taken steps to stabilize its balance sheet, its capital structure and earnings volatility still present elevated credit risk for mortgage and capital markets participants — including warehouse lenders and secondary market investors. Why the rating could shift in the future Fitch noted that its positive outlook could be revised to stable, or the CCC rating could be cut, if Finance of America fails to bolster its liquidity before upcoming maturities. Other factors that could drive a downgrade include deteriorating profitability and sustained leverage above 15s. The ratings agency said that FOA's ratio of total debt to tangible equity — excluding obligations tied to HECM Mortgage-Backed Securities (HMBS) and nonrecourse debt — was 33.7x at the end of September, up from 14.0x at the end of 2025. Fitch said it believes leverage will stay sensitive to interest rate movements. In December 2025, FOA issued $50 million of preferred stock to funds managed by Blue Owl Capital . Fitch treats these preferred shares as debt, since change-of-control provisions mandate redemption of the preferred shares in cash. But the agency said it does not believe the preferred shares will be a permanent part of FOA's capital structure as scheduled increases in coupons, starting with a 300-bps increase at the seventh anniversary date, provide an incentive to redeem and create an effective maturity. "We think it speaks a lot to the interest in the reverse segment, the fact that they’re willing to make an equity commitment to us and acquire the product that we’re generating," FOA CEO Graham Fleming told HousingWire 's Reverse Mortgage Daily earlier this year about the transaction. Fitch also noted potential upsides for FOA's ratings. These include sustained improvement in liquidity after near-term obligations are repaid, return on average assets being maintained above 1% with positive cash generation, and gross leverage staying below 10x. The agency also cited better funding flexibility through long-term and more committed facilities, growth that strengthens the FOA franchise brand, and deeper management expertise and clear succession planning as potential reasons to bolster the company's ratings down the road. items.title: Multifamily starts rose in October amid high borrowing, materials costs
items.description: Multifamily starts rose in October amid high borrowing, materials costs Although HUD and the U.S. Census Bureau data shows a monthly and yearly increase in apartment construction, “the broad landscape remains tepid,” according to an economist. Published Nov. 18, 2026 Julie Strupp Senior Editor Share Copy link Email LinkedIn X/Twitter Facebook Print License Add us on Google Drew Angerer via Getty Images Listen to the article 4 min This audio is auto-generated. Please let us know if you have feedback . Multifamily housing starts rose in October on a monthly and yearly basis, according to HUD and the U.S. Census Bureau’s latest residential construction report released Wednesday. In October, the seasonally adjusted starts rate for buildings with five or more units was 433,000, up 25.5% from September and up 22% year over year. Total privately owned housing starts stood at a seasonally adjusted rate of 1.309 million, 9.9% above September’s revised rate and 2.8% higher than October 2025. Single-family starts were at a rate of 864,000 in October, which is 4% above the revised September figure but 3.2% lower than the same period last year. Multifamily construction activity drove October’s increase, but “it is noteworthy that month-to-month construction data can be noisy and the broad landscape remains tepid,” according to George Ratiu, vice president of research at the National Apartment Association. “Builders are tracking slowing estimates of new households being formed and expecting the moderation to continue into 2027, as inflation and stagnant job market hamper Gen Z graduates from moving out,” Ratiu said in emailed comments. The number of apartment projects coming online continues to trend down. Multifamily project completions in October were at a seasonally adjusted rate of 362,000, 9% higher than September but 9% lower than the same period last year. Multifamily building permits, which signal future construction activity, stood at a seasonally adjusted rate of 120,000. That’s down 4% from September but up 7.1% YOY. There are 691,000 total apartment units currently under construction , per a Wednesday analysis from the National Association of Home Builders. However, “the market remains constrained by elevated borrowing costs, rising construction costs and weakening builder confidence,” said Danushka Nanayakkara-Skillington, NAHB’s assistant vice president for forecasting and analysis. Indeed, multifamily developer confidence weakened YOY in the third quarter, according to NAHB’s Nov. 5 Multifamily Market Survey. Regional differences Housing construction continues to be relatively strong in the South. That region saw the highest number of total starts in October with a seasonally adjusted rate of 747,000, up 12.2% YOY and up 10.5% month over month. The Midwest saw the biggest YOY increase, with starts up 17.2% from last October and up 48.4% from September. The Midwest’s total starts stood at a seasonally adjusted rate of 239,000 in October. By contrast, the Northeast saw the biggest YOY and MOM decline, with total starts at just 95,000 in October, down 34.5% and 20.8%, respectively. The West also saw starts fall on a monthly and yearly basis. They stood at 228,000 in October, down 11.6% YOY and down 2.6% MOM. The rising interest rate environment is making housing development more difficult in general, although “we’re seeing distinct differences depending upon the region you’re in,” Jay Lybik, senior director of market research at Continental Properties, previously told Multifamily Dive. High materials costs are also taxing builders , Construction Dive reported. Prices for construction inputs climbed 11.5% YOY in October, per an Associated Builders and Contractors analysis of Nov. 13 Producer Price Index data. That YOY surge is the biggest in more than four years, according to Associated General Contractors of America. “Construction firms are experiencing ever-greater impacts from tariff- and Middle East turmoil as prices accelerate for metals, fuel and freight,” Ken Simonson, AGC chief economist, said in a release. “In addition, lead times for steel and insulation have lengthened, making it harder for contractors to keep projects on schedule.” Click here to sign up to receive multifamily and apartment news like this article in your inbox every weekday. items.title: How apartment developers can successfully install connected services
items.description: How apartment developers can successfully install connected services Multifamily firms need to keep residents and staff front and center when putting Wi-Fi, access controls and other features into buildings, Cortland’s Duncan Cannon said at OPTECH. Published Nov. 18, 2026 Leslie Shaver Senior Reporter Share Copy link Email LinkedIn X/Twitter Facebook Print License Add us on Google Rental housing pros gathered at OPTECH 2026 in Las Vegas. Les Shaver/Multifamily Dive Listen to the article 4 min This audio is auto-generated. Please let us know if you have feedback . LAS VEGAS — There is no shortage of modern technology, such as managed Wi-Fi and smart-home features, that developers and renovators can put in apartment buildings. But before committing to those technologies, those groups must keep the residents front and center as they plan. “In pre-construction, it's really [about] what problem am I actually solving and how am I delivering that to the resident?” Duncan Cannon, senior director of building technology at Cortland, said on Monday at OPTECH 2026 in Las Vegas. “In multifamily, we are trying to deliver that experience to the residents.” In new developments, Mike Smith, president and CEO of WhiteSpace, agreed that stakeholders should be “asking questions around what is that end-user experience that you want to deliver.” Adding too many shiny bells and whistles can also lead to poor user experience. Cannon called some of the features being put into buildings “technology glitter” and said developers need to be cognizant of how they work with one another. “A lot of the point solutions don't necessarily tie to each other,” Cannon said. “You have [to have] the overall idea of what you want to deliver to those residents.” While user experience should be a guiding principle in connected buildings, staff education, accurate cost estimates and the selection of building components also matter a great deal. Staff education In redevelopment projects, such as those involving the installation of managed Wi-Fi, the operations team needs to be onboard, according to Cannon. “They need to understand what's happening,” Cannon said. “They need to understand the timeline because I promise you those residents will come in asking questions, and the more prepared they are to answer those questions, the better you will be set.” Changing access control also requires significant planning, according to Lisa Moore, senior director of community technology at Mill Creek Residential Trust. Last year, the company replaced door locks at roughly 600 units, according to Moore. Mill Creek needed its community team to educate residents. “We were constantly making sure that the community team was communicating when there would be tech on site at those particular units," Moore said. “The resident has to be involved in that process because the last thing you want them to do is show up home after work one night and have to deal with something that they weren't expecting to deal with.” The community team’s job doesn’t end after new door locks are installed or internet service is upgraded. Team members need frequent training on the systems to account for staff turnover at the property, according to Smith. Moore took it a step further, pointing out that operators should create their own documentation to supplement what vendors provide. “It [the vendor’s documentation] is never enough,” Moore said. “And we use our own documentation because it's just never really step-by-step enough for the actual community team.” Pricing, materials pitfalls Even if developers and owners keep staff and resident needs front and center when designing connected buildings, they can still run into problems. For instance, relying on a previous project’s costs to estimate a new project’s budget isn't the best strategy, according to Michael Doucette, vice president at Blueport, who also spoke at OPTECH. “In some cases, we see a lot of developers that have a number from a previous project associated with this new project, but it doesn't fit,” Doucette said. “It's not apples to apples. This [new building] might have a different amenity space, or this [property] has a different unit setup.” The choice of materials also matters. “You need to look at the components in detail,” Patrick Bailey, co-founder and senior vice president at ICS Advanced Technologies, said at OPTECH. “Everybody's gone through the days where we had copper-clad coax that didn't carry a signal very far.” Accounting for geographic differences is also important when planning how to heat and cool technology equipment, according to Bailey. “You have different requirements,” Bailey said. “In Arizona, you have to cool equipment. In Iowa, you don't necessarily have to cool it, but you do have to heat it in some cases.” Click here to sign up to receive multifamily and apartment news like this article in your inbox every weekday. items.title: 'Doesn't Look Good': October CRE Sales Volume Slumps, Setting Up Weak Q4
items.description: Commercial real estate sales volume took a dive in October after a strong third quarter, new data from MSCI and Altus Group shows. Unsplash/Clay LeConey CRE transaction volume totaled $35.4B in October, down 51% from last year, according to preliminary volume pricing data from MSCI released Wednesday. The last few months have included shake-ups to the capital markets landscape that are testing the resilience of CRE demand after what has until now been a relatively strong year for dealmaking across the asset class. Revisions to previously reported third-quarter data put transaction volume in the prior three months at $160.6B, up 16% from the prior year. There were no large mergers or entity deals in the quarter, which had boosted net sales volume in previous months. “There is still time for some improvement, especially as December is roughly 15% of the full year,” JPMorgan Chase analysts wrote in a note to investors Wednesday morning, noting that December typically sees outsized transaction activity. “But again, the start to the quarter doesn’t look good.” The average cap rate for all transactions was 6.85% in October, up 15 basis points from September. Retail saw the largest swing in cap rates, with a 16-basis-point push upward to 7.20%, while office was up 9 basis points to 7.46%, apartments ticked up 7 basis points to 8.22% and industrial assets saw cap rates rise 3 basis points to 6.6%, according to MSCI. Buyers and sellers seem to be quickly adjusting to the interest rate environment, and fundamentals still look broadly solid, the JPMorgan analysts wrote. The MSCI data comes as a third-quarter report from Altus Group, the maker of the ubiquitous CRE software Argus, released Wednesday showed momentum had been building in capital markets. Transaction volume by dollars spent was up 19.7% quarter-over-quarter and 20.3% year-over-year, with the number of properties sold also up by 3.8% and 6.9%, respectively, according to the report . The median price per square foot across all asset types was up 2.3% from the second quarter and 7.8% from a year ago. Deals valued at $10M or more accounted for more than two-thirds of total dollar volume, and the data suggests that deals are starting to concentrate in higher-priced, larger assets. “Industrial and office trades drove the momentum through the third quarter, despite the rise in interest rates,” Cole Perry, associate director of research at Altus Group, said in a statement. “While the shift toward larger transactions suggests capital is becoming more willing to move when investors see quality and conviction in the opportunity.” The last few months have included shake-ups to the capital markets landscape that will test the resilience of CRE demand in the fourth quarter. Yields for 10-year U.S. Treasury bonds first cleared 5% in September , shortly before the Federal Reserve raised its benchmark interest rate for the first time since 2023. Shares of tech stocks in the booming world of artificial intelligence were already slumping before the bombshell ouster of Jensen Huang , Nvidia ’s former CEO and one of the most prolific voices in the AI race, earlier this month pushed them down further. items.title: Pending Home Sales Tumble to New Record Low as High Mortgage Rates Freeze Buyers
items.description: Pending home sales descended to a new all-time low in October as mortgage rates surged to a three-year peak , keeping would-be buyers firmly on the sidelines. Contract signings fell 4.7% compared to September, and plummeted 16.7% year over year, according to the National Association of Realtors® Pending Home Sales report released on Wednesday. "October could mark the low point in contract signings for this housing cycle, as mortgage rates appear to have topped out," says NAR Chief Economist Lawrence Yun . The October readout comes on the heels of the previous record low set in September , when pending sales fell 7.3% month over month and 11.3% year over year. "Two consecutive months of record-low pending contracts point to very sluggish fourth-quarter home sales closings, and annual existing-home sales could be the lowest since the mid-1990s," says Yun. Same as in September, pending sales were down both month over month and year over year in all four U.S. regions. The West saw the largest monthly pullback with a 6.9% drop, followed by the South (-6.3%), Midwest (-2.7%), and Northeast (-0.8%). Annually, the West was again at the forefront with a 20.3% drop, followed by the South (-18.7%), Midwest (-14%), and Northeast (-11.1%). "Even though all four regions saw dramatic cooling, the relative strength of the Midwest and Northeast are clear, due largely to still-scarce inventory conditions," says Realtor.com® senior economist Hannah Jones . At the metro level, pending sales fell year over year even in the hitherto most resilient markets. Across the 50 largest metros, the smallest decreases were recorded in Cincinnati, OH (-4.7% year over year), Austin, TX (-9.7%), and Hartford, CT (-10%). Loading... "It is somewhat puzzling that home sales would fall to levels last seen three decades ago, even as the U.S. population has grown by roughly 75 million," notes Yun. "Either sizable housing demand is building in the background, or the dream of homeownership is increasingly out of reach for many Americans." On Oct. 8, the average rate on 30-year fixed home loans reached 7.40%, the highest since Nov. 2023, eroding buyers' purchasing power. Rates have since retreated, but October’s hot inflation data released last week is expected to push them higher again. "Until inflation cools enough to put mortgage rates on a downward path, affordability problems are likely to persist, keeping contract signings and home sales subdued," says Jones. Metros with the smallest pending sales declines in October Cincinnati, OH (-4.7%) Austin, TX (-9.7%) Hartford, CT(-10%) Indianapolis, IN (-11.3%) Chicago, IL (-11.9%) Pittsburgh, PA (-6.2%) Nashville, TN (-12.7%) Buffalo, NY (-12.7%) Jacksonville, FL (-12.8%) Cleveland, OH (-12.8%) What this means for buyers this fall Jones suggests that while uncertainty preceding the November midterm elections may have played a role in stalling homebuying activity, she strongly believes that surging mortgage rates were the more likely culprit. Mortgage rates climbed nearly 75 basis points from late August to mid-October, adding roughly $200 a month to the typical mortgage payment on a median-priced home, assuming a 10% down payment. "That is more than many already-strained buyers can easily absorb," argues Jones. According to the economist, affordability remains the limiting factor in today’s housing market. The typical mortgage-holder would see a $1,100 increase in their monthly payment if they bought a median-priced home today. While sellers have shown some flexibility, with lower asking prices and more price cuts , buyers have not responded with much enthusiasm at these rates. "Sellers are only willing to come down so far and buyers are only willing to stretch so far, and a gap still separates the two," adds Jones. As a result, transaction volume in October hit its lowest level in 16 years . However, there are upsides for buyers who can afford to act: less competition, more homes to choose from, and sellers who are willing to negotiate. Snejana Farberov is a reporter at Realtor.com covering the U.S. housing market and the latest domestic real estate trends. She has worked as a general assignment journalist in New York City and Long Island for 16 years, writing for New York Post, Daily Mail, and News 12. Snejana earned bachelor's degrees in journalism and Italian from St. John's University, followed by a master’s degree from Columbia University School of Journalism.

items.title: Fitch warns of growing balance-sheet strain at top nonbank mortgage firms
items.description: Fitch Ratings revised its outlooks on three major nonbank mortgage companies to negative and warned that elevated leverage and growing mortgage servicing rights (MSR) exposure are weighing on credit profiles in a higher-for-longer rate environment. In a periodic review of nine publicly rated nonbank mortgage firms released Monday, Fitch affirmed all long-term issuer default ratings but shifted the outlooks for Pennymac Financial Services , Planet Financial Group and Freedom Mortgage Holdings to negative from stable. Fitch maintained the following long-term issuer default ratings: Onity Group at B-, UWM Holdings Corp. at B+, Pennymac at BB, Planet at B, CrossCountry Mortgage at BB-, Rocket Companies at BBB-, Freedom at BB-, Finance of America at CCC and Provident Funding Associates at B. Fitch said profitability for several lenders is likely to be constrained in 2027, given a challenging rate backdrop that limits refinance volume and makes it harder for companies to retain earnings and pay down debt . That dynamic is expected to pressure leverage ratios across the sector. Three negative outlooks At Pennymac , corporate leverage has exceeded Fitch’s 1.5x downgrade trigger since the first quarter of 2026. And a failure to make meaningful progress toward reducing corporate leverage to 1.5x or less over the outlook horizon could lead to a downgrade to BB-, Fitch said. “Fitch expects profitability to be constrained in 2027 by a challenging rate environment and the lag in realizing the full impact of recent expense reduction initiatives,” Fitch stated. For Planet , the agency pointed to a significant increase in MSR exposure since 2021, as the company retained servicing from its own originations and acquired bulk portfolios. MSRs represented about 363% of company equity in the second quarter of 2026, up from 293% a year earlier and above the level of higher-rated peers, Fitch said. Planet’s corporate leverage also rose to 5.5x, up from 4.3x during the same period. Fitch considers that level high and a key constraint on the rating. The agency said it could downgrade Planet if leverage rises above its 7.0x trigger. At Freedom , corporate leverage — measured as gross nonfunding debt to tangible equity — reached Fitch’s 2.0x downgrade trigger in the second quarter, up from 1.9x at the end of 2025. Shareholder distributions exceeded earnings in the first half of the year, contributing to the increase. Fitch expects Freedom’s leverage to rise further as it grows its servicing portfolio and uses available borrowing capacity to meet potential margin calls under its hedging program. A closer look at top lenders At UWM , Fitch cited high leverage, MSR valuation risk and reliance on short-term, largely uncommitted secured funding as constraints on its rating. Corporate leverage, excluding origination funding, climbed to 5.3x in the third quarter of 2026, nearly double the 2.7x figure at the end of 2025. MSR mark-to-market volatility and a $603 million hedge loss in the second quarter have weighed on profitability. Still, Fitch pointed to a 30% adjusted EBITDA margin for the trailing 12 months through the third quarter as evidence of solid core earnings. “Fitch expects leverage to decline over time, supported by planned MSR sales and earnings above the expected $165 million annual preferred dividend. Common dividends are suspended. items.title: Real REMAX Group confirms additional layoffs after merger
items.description: After a merger or acquisition closes, companies almost always look for cost synergies. These efforts frequently result in layoffs, which they did at the recently formed Real REMAX Group , a RealTrends Verified firm. During the company’s third-quarter 2026 earnings call with investors and analysts, which occurred a little over two months after The Real Brokerage closed its acquisition of REMAX , executives said the company reduced its combined headcount by more than 14%, eliminating 150-plus positions across the combined organization. This came as the company said it found more than $40 million in annualized gross cost savings and expects to realize more than $30 million in adjusted EBITDA savings in 2027, which could increase to more than $40 million in 2028. At the time of the earnings call, executives said the initial phase of headcount restructuring was largely complete but that they were still looking for ways to simplify operations and improve efficiencies. But based on a recent slew of posts on LinkedIn , it appears that headcount reductions are not over just yet. Over the past week, several individuals who claim to be former REMAX employees shared posts stating that they'd been impacted by a recent round of layoffs at the company. A spokesperson for Real REMAX Group told HousingWire via email that following the acquisition, “Real REMAX Group is continuing to evaluate opportunities that streamline operations, create efficiencies and better integrate the two organizations.” “As part of this ongoing process, we can confirm that additional organizational changes have taken place at the company,” the spokesperson wrote. “We will continue to assess our business needs to ensure we have the right structure and resources in place to support our long-term strategic priorities and better serve real estate professionals.” The spokesperson declined to share details regarding the size of the layoffs, which departments were impacted or if the layoffs were performance related. Real REMAX Group is not alone in laying off employees as part of an attempt to rightsize after a merger. Earlier this year, Compass International Holdings announced it was laying off 110 employees after it closed its acquisition of Anywhere Real Estate . Compass has estimated $500 million in total net cost synergies over the next three years. Related More: Mergers and Acquisitions Mortgage and Housing Layoffs REMAX The Real Brokerage

items.title: Why buyers may get more from seller concessions than a price cut
items.description: Contract signings dropped 7.3% in September, pushing the National Association of Realtors' Pending Home Sales Index to its lowest level since the index began in 2001. Signings were down 11.3% from a year earlier. October brought no relief. Redfin's weekly data for the four weeks ending Nov. 1 shows pending sales down 16.4% year over year, the lowest level in its records, with declines in every major metro it tracks. With mortgage rates still above 7%, the buyers who remain in the market are dealing with sellers who need them far more than they did a year ago. Most of those buyers will spend their leverage on the asking price. The instinct makes sense, and it often leaves the more valuable concession unclaimed. Buyers should approach this negotiation as a financing decision. That is usually where the larger savings sit. Which markets favor buyers The national numbers hide a market that is splitting by region. In Redfin’s data from late October , Seattle, San Diego, Atlanta, Denver and Las Vegas posted the steepest pending-sales declines, each down between 22.6% and 30.5% from a year earlier. Sale prices have already fallen in Austin, Seattle and Fort Lauderdale. In September, Redfin found that nearly one in five contracts was canceled in Jacksonville, Tampa, Las Vegas, San Antonio and Phoenix. Sellers in those markets are watching listings age and deals unravel. They will take a request for closing costs seriously. San Francisco is another story, with its median sale price up 17.3% year over year. Nassau County, NY, and Montgomery County, PA, are still classified as seller's markets, and contracts there rarely fall through. Buyers in those areas can ask for concessions, but they should expect a shorter answer. For everyone else, local days on market and the share of listings with price cuts offer the best read on how hard to push. Nationally, 21.2% of listings carried a price drop in the latest Redfin data. A home that has sat well past the local median, with a cut or two behind it, belongs to a seller who is ready to talk. Why a lower price does less than buyers expect Consider a $600,000 home bought with 20% down at a 7.25% rate. A $10,000 price reduction shrinks the down payment by $2,000 and the loan to $472,000, bringing monthly principal and interest from roughly $3,271 to $3,217. The buyer saves about $55 a month. If the buyer takes a $10,000 seller credit toward closing costs instead, the price holds at $600,000. Compared with the price cut, they walk away from closing with about $8,000 more in their pocket. At $55 a month, the price reduction needs around 12 years to catch up. Few buyers keep the same loan that long, and a buyer who refinances when rates come down will likely never reach the breakeven point. Sellers often prefer the credit too. Their net proceeds come out about the same, and a credit keeps the recorded sale price intact for the comps that will shape their neighbors' values. That makes it an easier concession to win. Price, however, is still important. A lower purchase price reduces the interest paid over the life of the loan and starts the buyer with more equity. With rates this high, few buyers will keep the same loan for 15 years without refinancing, but those who plan to could reasonably weigh price more heavily. The home also has to appraise at the contract price. If it comes in low, a concession won’t close the gap, and the buyer may need a price reduction anyway. Matching the ask to what the buyer needs Closing-cost credits are the simplest use of a concession, but buyers focused on the monthly payment can put the same money toward a rate buydown. A temporary 2-1 buydown lowers the rate by two percentage points in the first year and one in the second. Discount points lower it for the life of the loan. In the example above, $10,000 in points could take roughly half a percentage point off the rate, depending on lender pricing. That works out to about $160 a month, nearly triple what the price cut delivers. Buyers can also ask for both. Going back to the $600,000 home, suppose the buyer wants to pay $560,000. Asking the seller for a $40,000 credit is a big request, and it would likely exceed the buyer’s total closing costs. A $30,000 price reduction paired with the same $10,000 concession gets the buyer to their number, and a seller is more likely to agree to two moderate asks than one large one. How that concession gets used depends on where the buyer feels the pressure. Buyers stretching to cover cash at closing may get more from credits, while those with a tight monthly budget may be better served by a buydown. Credits also have formal limits. Conventional loans cap seller contributions at 3% to 9% of the price depending on the down payment, and FHA allows up to 6%. Any credit beyond the buyer’s eligible closing costs goes unused, and non-QM programs vary widely by lender. Buyers should structure financing before the offer goes in so they know exactly how much credit they can use. Negotiate the whole deal The most motivated sellers right now are the ones watching their listings sit in markets where buyers keep walking away. What they want most is a contract that makes it to closing. A buyer who arrives with the financing already worked out can offer that certainty and should expect the seller to pay for it. Buyers who negotiate only on price in this market are likely shortchanging themselves. So are buyers who treat price and concessions as an either/or choice. In the few metros where things remain competitive, the leverage is yet to materialize. Across most of the country, buyers have room to ask for both. items.title: Congress Puts Up $216M For Energy Department Relocation From Forrestal
items.description: The Department of Energy’s 1.8M SF office complex along Independence Avenue is one step closer to its next chapter. A Senate committee approved $215.6M in funding Wednesday to relocate the agency’s employees from the James V. Forrestal trio of office buildings into its next headquarters. The funds can be used to prepare Forrestal for disposition and Energy's new headquarters for its habitation, according to a resolution from the Senate’s Environment and Public Works Committee. The 1960s-era Forrestal complex at 1000 Independence Ave. SW acts as a massive physical barrier between the National Mall and the Wharf. Its redevelopment has long been viewed by urban planners as a key component in unlocking a mixed-use vision for D.C.'s southwest federal corridor. Google Maps The Department of Energy's James V. Forrestal Building at 1000 Independence Ave. SW The funding will go to the federal government’s landlord, the General Services Administration , via its FY2026 Optimization Program Prospectus. The EPW Committee passed that prospectus Wednesday, and a House panel approved the funding in July . The GSA announced in March that Energy would be clearing out of Forrestal and moving into the Department of Education’s 50-year-old headquarters: the Lyndon B. Johnson Building on Maryland Avenue Southwest. Education, in turn, announced that it would move into a building at 500 D St. SW, which was previously leased for the now largely defunct U.S. Agency for International Development. That move, expected to cut Education's footprint by 80%, was set to be completed in August. The GSA said in a Wednesday news release that the relocation money allows the agency “to consider alternative uses for the Forrestal Building, including disposition.” The GSA didn’t provide a timeline for when the move will begin or how long it should take. Its press office didn’t respond to Bisnow ’s request for information. GSA Administrator Edward Forst said in the release that the move will “reduce waste, avoid more than $350 million in delinquent maintenance costs, and deliver a workplace that better serves agencies, employees, and the American taxpayer.” In September, a Government Accountability Office report said the agency would need funding to “fit out classified space to meet Energy’s mission needs” at its new LBJ Building home. Momentum has been building over the past two years to transform the 230 acres that make up D.C.’s southwest federal corridor into a new mixed-use neighborhood. The federal government this year offloaded its first two federal properties in the corridor : the Regional Office Building and the Liberty Loan Building on the Tidal Basin. It has earmarked other large headquarters buildings for disposition but this summer seemed to quietly pull back on those efforts, the Washington Business Journal reported . Public and private stakeholders have worried about the lack of a coherent vision and plan for the neighborhood. The first sign that a formal planning document was underway came last month when Diane Sullivan, the acting executive director of the National Capital Planning Commission, presented a preliminary vision for the neighborhood, broken into three districts, each with a distinct focus: residential, arts and culture, and federal office. Under that vision, Forrestal, which sits across from the Smithsonian’s Arts and Industries Building, would be included in the 10th Street Cultural/Entertainment District. items.title: Fed Officials Expect Further Interest Rate Hikes After Pausing Last Month
items.description: Leaders at the Federal Reserve held firm on interest rates in October, but also felt a future rate hike "would likely be appropriate" as some mulled a larger hike in December, according to meeting minutes released Wednesday. At the Oct. 27-28 meeting of the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC), policymakers voted 10-2 to keep the overnight rate at its previous 3.75%-4% range. The decision came days before the 2026 midterms, even as FOMC members agreed inflation was a persistent concern, Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh joined the majority, while Fed Gov. Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack , both voted in favor of a quarter-point increase. One month before, the FOMC voted to raise rates for the first time in three years in an effort to clamp down on inflation. The minutes—which don't name FOMC members specifically while discussing their deliberations—show that some of the FOMC members considered that, while the impact of tariffs on the economy was waning, high energy costs continue to pressure Americans. Indeed, some participants even noted that, if the inflation numbers got too unfavorable, they would consider a rate hike of more than a quarter-percent in December. Bond markets still view that as unlikely, with the probability of a larger half-point hike next month at just 5%, according to CME FedWatch . Still, Federal Reserve Gov. Christopher Waller told CNBC Wednesday it may be necessary to "shock people" with a larger rate hike. He said in a speech this month that a half-percent point hike might be necessary next month. "Inflation's been above our target for over five years, so if you really want to get it down you have to start taking more aggressive actions," Waller told CNBC. December rate hike looks all but certain FOMC members also said the rapid artificial intelligence buildout was contributing to inflation. But more scrutiny of the industry could slow spending and reduce inflation pressures. Those members later determined holding rates steady at the October meeting would allow for time to "assess the durability of AI-related investment demand, the evolution of financing conditions, the transmission of the September rate increase to the economy, or geopolitical developments." "A couple of participants noted that, at the current juncture, a gradual approach to policy firming would give businesses and households time to adjust to higher interest rates," the minutes state. Inflation remained hot in October. Overall prices rose 0.4% from September , according to the Consumer Price Index (CPI) data released by the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) last week. Some numbers look better. After a disappointing September , U.S. payrolls came roaring back in October as employers added 165,000 new jobs , pushing the unemployment rate down to 4.1%. CME FedWatch currently prices a roughly 95% chance of the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) raising the federal funds to a 4%-4.25% range in December, followed by a 69% probability of 4.25%-4.5% in January. The meeting minutes show that Fed leaders are aware that public sentiment broadly expects the December rate hike. "Some participants," the minutes state, judge those estimates to be "broadly consistent with their assessments of the appropriate policy rate path." Several of the meeting members also said it was a "close call." In the meantime, Cook and Hammack said that inflation remained too high and they didn't see enough signs that it was letting up. They worried that delaying the rate hike any further could risk higher inflation becoming entrenched. That, in turn, could mean more drastic rate hikes in the future. More rate hikes in the cards Waller isn't the only Fed leader saying that the market needs more than one quarter-point rate hike. "The economy will likely require several interest rate increases before the spring of 2027 to achieve 2% inflation in a timely manner," St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem said this week at a conference in Argentina. Realtor.com Chief Economist Danielle Hale said the market ultimately anticipates two or three hikes over the next 6 to 8 months. The Market has reacted. Pending home sales in September dropped to their lowest level on record . "While the market and the Fed both seem to agree that some monetary policy restriction is warranted, most investors currently expect more restriction than the Fed has projected," Hale said last month. But there is still an opportunity for homebuyers in this environment. Hale recommended homebuyers set themselves up for a better mortgage rate by boosting credit, making a higher down payment, and shopping around for a mortgage. Tristan Navera is a senior reporter on housing policy, covering trends and solutions in the housing market from Washington, DC. He was previously a senior reporter at Bloomberg Law, and before that covered real estate for the Washington Business Journal. Earlier in his career, he spent a decade reporting on business and real estate in Dayton and Columbus, OH. A Cincinnati native, he holds a journalism degree from Ohio University.

items.title: Sherwood Equities Sells Hudson Yards Development Site For $100M: The N.Y. Deal Sheet
items.description: Long before Hudson Yards was the buzzy hot spot it is today, Sherwood Equities snapped up a 17K SF parcel of land at 460 10th Ave. And this week, it sold it to Joyland Group for $100M, Commercial Observer first reported . Google Maps The site at 460 10th Ave. is now slated to become housing. Sherwood had owned the residential development site since the 1990s, according to the firm’s website . It is unclear why Sherwood sold the property, but it once had plans to build more than 200 apartments on the site, according to The Real Deal . As recently as February, Sherwood agreed to add affordable housing to the site and invest $11.8M in neighborhood infrastructure upgrades in exchange for tacking on another 70K SF to the development, according to plans filed with the Department of Buildings. Now, a partnership between Joyland and Prospect Development has big plans for the site, Commercial Observer reported. The duo wants to build a 34-story, 456-unit apartment building. JLL’s Jonathan Hageman, Ethan Stanton, Andrew Scandalios, Hall Oster, Michael Mazzara and Brendan Maddigan represented Sherwood in the sale. The property had been on the market for a little over a year, according to an announcement on the brokerage’s website. TOP SALES Tishman Realty sold a 50K SF parking garage at 112 E. 16th St. to Pro-H Development for $44.3M, Crain's New York Business reported . The garage, which sits between Irving Place and Union Square East, will likely be demolished to make way for housing. Tishman representatives had filed permits to build a 22-story, 52-unit mixed-use building before the sale, with the new owner planning to turn the 52 units into for-sale homes. *** Trammell Crow Co. acquired 442 W. 18th St., a lot with a vacant two-story garage and office building, for $67.5M, PincusCo reported . The seller was family-owned Retaco Holding, which had owned the site since 1983. The new owner plans to build a 14-story mixed-use residential and commercial building. JLL’s Jonathan Hageman, Steven Rutman and Tyler Peck worked with Institutional Property Advisors’ Steven Siegel and Eric Anton to arrange the off-market deal for Retaco, Commercial Observer reported . *** Namdar Realty Group and Mason Asset Management snagged a 132K SF office building at 71 Fifth Ave. for $60.6M, PincusCo reported . Namdar and Mason borrowed $42M from Truist Bank to finance the purchase. The sellers were Madison Capital and Lubert-Adler. TOP LEASES Google Maps GFP's 520 Eighth Ave., where the Mason Tenders’ District Council Trust Funds is staying put for another 10 years Mason Tenders’ District Council Trust Funds renewed its 40K SF lease at GFP Real Estate’s 520 Eighth Ave. for another 10 years, according to a release. The organization has been in the 1926-built, 860K SF building since 2001 and plans to continue to use the property as its administrative offices. GFP’s Matthew Mandell handled the transaction in-house without any outside brokerages. *** MD Squared Property Group leased 16K SF at The Feil Organization’s 145 W. 30th St., bringing the property to 100% leased, according to a release. The deal follows Feil’s announcement that Turner School had renewed its 8K SF lease on the sixth floor of the 12-story office. Andrew Wiener represented the landlord in-house, while MD Squared represented itself. *** Nonprofit Child Center of NY inked a 16K SF lease at Stellar Management’s 35-01 36th Ave. in Astoria, Commercial Observer reported . Asking rents for the 10-year deal at the nine-story building were $50 per SF. Sholom & Zuckerbrot’s Gail Roseman represented the tenant, while NY Space Finders’ Luca DiCiero and Faisal Gilani represented the landlord. Coworking firm International Workplace Group, which signed for 8K SF in January 2025, is the building’s anchor. *** Activate Games signed a 16K SF lease at Acadia Realty Trust’s Downtown Brooklyn mall, City Point, Crain’s New York Business reported . The live-action video game experience company will occupy a ground-floor, mezzanine and lower-level space. The store is expected to open in June. Momentum Realty Group’s Chandler Slate represented the tenant. TOP FINANCING Google Maps 21-12 30th Road in Astoria, where Mega Contracting Group scored a $256.3M loan to develop hundreds of homes Mega Contracting Group scored a $256.3M construction loan for a 236-unit mixed-use project at 21-12 30th Road in Astoria, PincusCo reported . The funding came from a group of lenders including TD Bank, Enterprise Community Partners, NYC Department of Housing Preservation and Development and the NYS Housing Finance Agency. The property has an alternative address of 30-37 21st St. *** Wells Fargo provided a $258.2M loan to L+M Development Partners to refinance three apartment buildings in East Harlem, PincusCo reported . The properties span 1M SF across 761 units. They are located at 1962 and 1940 First Ave. and 455 E. 102nd St. The debt retires a $232.1M Fannie Mae loan. *** Artifact and Ashok Khuban netted two refinancing loans totaling $147.5M and covering three rental buildings in Upper Manhattan, PincusCo reported . Bank of Montreal provided the financing. The first loan, valued at $94M, was for 636-646 W. 158th St. and retires a $85.5M sum. The second loan, a $53.5M sum, was for 1871-1873 and 1867 Amsterdam Ave. and replaces a $46.2M sum. The prior lender in both cases was Genesis Capital. recent_coverage.summary_zh: 高力国际称，2026 年第 3 季度美国多户住宅入住率升至 95.7%，净吸纳低于新增交付，开发管线继续收缩；60 个主要市场中有 40 个租金同比上涨。

recent_coverage.title: Builder Sentiment Continues to Fall on Affordability Concerns
recent_coverage.summary_zh: NAHB 与富国银行的 11 月住房市场指数下降 4 点至 25，为 2012 年 4 月以来最低。调查显示，46% 的建商降价，68% 提供销售优惠；NAHB 指出，建商正在缩减施工规模。

recent_coverage.title: MarketBeat SF Bay Area Multifamily Q3 2026
recent_coverage.summary_zh: 戴德梁行称，2026 年第 3 季度旧金山湾区多户住宅空置率连降 12 个季度至 3.9%，季末有效租金同比上涨近 10%，在建量连续第 5 个季度上升至 18,625 套。

recent_coverage.title: Onyx+East, EJF Capital to Develop $17.5M Build-to-Rent Community in Indianapolis
recent_coverage.summary_zh: Onyx+East 与 EJF Capital 敲定合资开发，总投资 1,750 万美元的 Monon 21 将建 57 套出租住宅。项目已完成拆除并开始场地准备，计划于 2028 年底完工。

recent_coverage.title: LAHSA To Return $150M Of HUD Funding In Finalized Settlement
recent_coverage.summary_zh: 联邦法官签署和解协议，要求洛杉矶无家可归者服务管理局退还约 1.5 亿美元联邦资金。资金将分阶段转由洛杉矶县管理，地区每年 2.4 亿美元的住房服务拨款申请得以保留。

recent_coverage.title: Promise Robotics raises $25M to scale automated homebuilding
recent_coverage.summary_zh: Promise Robotics 宣布获 2,500 万美元 B 轮融资，此前已与 D.R. Horton 签订多年协议，支持其建造超过 1,250 套住宅。公司计划于 2027 年启用凤凰城工厂。

recent_coverage.title: Custom Home Building Share Rises in 2025
recent_coverage.summary_zh: NAHB 援引美国人口普查局调查称，定制住宅占独栋住宅开工的比重从 2024 年的 17.5% 升至 2025 年的 19.6%；2025 年开工的独栋住宅中，8.6% 为出租而建。

recent_coverage.title: Westcore Entity Pays $51.1M for Seattle-Area Light Industrial Campus
recent_coverage.summary_zh: Westcore 关联实体从黑石旗下 Link Logistics 收购西雅图以东伍丁维尔的一处多租户轻工业园，交易金额据报道为 5,110 万美元。

recent_coverage.title: New-Construction Insights: Builders Hold Steady on Price, but Offer Savings via Reduced Rates
recent_coverage.summary_zh: Realtor.com 称，美国新屋挂牌中位价近 3 年基本持平。按房价 40 万美元、首付 10% 测算，得益于利率优惠，新屋买家首年利息平均每月比典型成屋买家少 258 美元。

recent_coverage.title: Big V Property Group Acquires 7.4-Acre Parcel in Anna, Texas, for Retail Expansion Project
recent_coverage.summary_zh: Big V 在达拉斯以北的安纳收购 7.4 英亩地块，紧邻其在建购物中心 Rosamond Town Center，并从一家地区银行获得 1,100 万美元收购及建设贷款。

recent_coverage.title: First liens may lag until 4Q27 as cash-outs, seconds compete
recent_coverage.summary_zh: 据 National Mortgage News 报道，房利美虽将按揭利率预测下调至 7.2%，仍预计按揭业务量疲弱将持续至 2027 年第 3 季度，部分放贷机构正转向第二顺位按揭。

recent_coverage.title: ARCTRUST, Edison Equity Break Ground on 175-Unit Active Adult Community in Metro Austin
recent_coverage.summary_zh: ARCTRUST 与 Edison Equity 在奥斯汀西南部启动 Serenova 长者社区建设。项目共 175 套住宅，面向 55 岁及以上住户，计划于 2028 年秋季完工。

recent_coverage.title: FASB rule could push community banks to sell servicing
recent_coverage.summary_zh: 据 National Mortgage News 报道，美国财务会计准则委员会拟议的会计标准可能使部分金融机构更难评估按揭服务权价值，社区银行或因此出售相关服务权。

recent_coverage.title: Single-Family Permitting Weakens While Multifamily Activity Remains Stronger
recent_coverage.summary_zh: NAHB 数据显示，2026 年截至 September 的年初至今，美国独栋住宅许可为 689,884 套，同比下降 3.0%；多户许可为 393,778 套，同比增长 4.1%。

recent_coverage.title: Hedge fund pressures Invitation Homes to speed up home sales
recent_coverage.summary_zh: Land & Buildings 敦促 Invitation Homes 加快售房、增加资本返还并收缩增长计划。该投资者认为公司股价显著低于住宅价值，其估值判断尚非已实现交易结果。

recent_coverage.title: Where Developers Are Trying To Lease Public Lands To Build Data Centers
recent_coverage.summary_zh: Bisnow 核查发现，美国联邦机构正考虑出租至少 17 块公共土地，合计 19,200 英亩，用于数据中心及电力基础设施；相关项目处于已获批或待授权阶段。

recent_coverage.title: Service Properties Trust Rejects $2B Cash Bid, Claims Hotel Portfolio Could Be Worth Double
recent_coverage.summary_zh: Service Properties Trust 拒绝 20 亿美元酒店资产报价，计划保留 77 家酒店至明年起出售。董事会寄望盈利改善抬升售价，但第三季度净亏损扩大、每股运营资金下降。

recent_coverage.title: Who Owns Outright? Mortgage Status, Lock-In and Senior Homeownership
recent_coverage.summary_zh: Realtor.com 研究显示，2025 年美国自住房中 41% 无按揭；75 岁及以上业主的无按揭比例则较 2010 年下降。研究认为，低息贷款锁定效应可能影响代际住房交接时点。

recent_coverage.title: Blackstone's Data Center REIT Makes First Investment With $5B AWS Deal
recent_coverage.summary_zh: 黑石旗下 BXDC 拟收购两家 AWS 合资企业的 75% 股权，交易估值 50 亿美元。组合由亚马逊全额回租，初始三净租期 12 年，租金获 AWS 担保，预计年底前交割。

recent_coverage.title: Lenders increasingly pull with new credit score model, but few use it for pricing
recent_coverage.summary_zh: 美国银行研究显示，调用 VantageScore 4.0 的贷款机构增多，但多数仍以 Classic FICO 定价；10 月新模型定价约占常规发行量的 8%，采用主要集中于 Rocket 和 UWM。

recent_coverage.title: Fed warns of financial risks from AI-driven market optimism
recent_coverage.summary_zh: 美联储在周五的半年度金融稳定报告中再次将资产高估值列为主要风险，并指出数据中心开发企业、信贷市场、私人贷款人与特殊目的融资工具的复杂关联需密切监测。

recent_coverage.title: IPA Arranges $40.3M in Financing for North San Antonio Apartment Community
recent_coverage.summary_zh: IPA 为圣安东尼奥北部 Birwood Heights 公寓安排 4,030 万美元融资。该项目建于 2019 年，共 312 套住宅，贷款期限为 3 年，采用无追索权结构。

recent_coverage.title: Nearly Two-Thirds of Phoenix-Area Residents Have Considered Moving Because of Housing Costs, New Survey Finds
recent_coverage.summary_zh: NRHC 公布的凤凰城地区调查显示，65% 受访居民曾因住房成本考虑搬迁，租户中该比例为 77%；55% 支持增建出租住宅，反映可负担性压力与新增住房支持并存。

recent_coverage.title: America’s Trillion-Dollar Credit Card Debt Threatens To Lock Millions Out of the Housing Market
recent_coverage.summary_zh: 纽约联储数据显示，第三季度信用卡余额增至创纪录的 1.29 万亿美元，同比增长 4.2%。报道援引贷款业人士指出，高消费债务对储蓄较少、财务空间较紧的首次购房者影响更大。

recent_coverage.title: Stream Realty Partners Brokers Sale of 2.7 MSF Industrial Park in Northwest Houston
recent_coverage.summary_zh: Adkisson Group 与 PCCP 合资企业收购休斯敦西北部 Northwoods 工业园，面积 270 万平方英尺，成交时出租率为 98%；IPA 同时安排收购融资及合资结构。

recent_coverage.title: The Tuccori commission settlements were supposed to wrap up, then the judge asked for more
recent_coverage.summary_zh: Tuccori 购房佣金诉讼和解尚未获最终批准。法院要求补充说明和解金额的确定方式、公平性、被告支付能力及继续诉讼的潜在回收额，相关主体的诉讼不确定性延续。

recent_coverage.title: Shorenstein Acquires 300,000 SF Office Tower in North Dallas
recent_coverage.summary_zh: Shorenstein 收购达拉斯北部 30 万平方英尺的 Sherry Lane Place 办公楼。项目近期已升级会议及租户设施，买方计划继续改造大堂、户外座席并增设配套。

recent_coverage.title: Why analysts have a less rosy outlook for banks in 2027
recent_coverage.summary_zh: 美国货币监理署在半年度风险报告中警示人工智能热潮相关风险，指出数据中心融资采用的新型金融和合同结构，在压力环境下的表现记录有限。

recent_coverage.title: Amid ‘economic headwinds,’ Boston looks to ease its inclusionary zoning policy
recent_coverage.summary_zh: 波士顿市长提议降低开发商代缴费用、延长可负担住房付款安排，并暂将多户住宅适用门槛由 7 套提高至 10 套。市府称方案旨在降低前期成本、改善开发可行性。

recent_coverage.title: Waterfall Originates Loan for Disneyland Lodging Property
recent_coverage.summary_zh: Waterfall 向 Dynamic City Capital 提供 4,800 万美元优先抵押贷款，为阿纳海姆 Portofino 酒店再融资。资金将用于偿还原贷款及改造，该酒店拥有 190 间客房。

recent_coverage.title: Realpage’s New York lawsuit tests the limits of algorithmic rent-pricing bans
recent_coverage.summary_zh: RealPage 挑战纽约州住宅租金算法禁令的诉讼持续。法律专家认为，案件可能厘清地方监管此类技术与商业言论保护之间的界限，但最终裁决的影响仍难估计。

recent_coverage.title: Craig Hall Is Betting on the Future of Office. His Next Chapter at HALL Park Is Taking Shape.
recent_coverage.summary_zh: HALL Group 正推进弗里斯科 HALL Park 下一阶段，包括甲级办公楼、公园扩建及住宅开发。项目近期获得摩根大通承诺入驻及 Public Storage 总部迁入，租赁动能回升。

recent_coverage.title: Realpage Economy Express Episode 75
recent_coverage.summary_zh: RealPage 援引劳工统计局数据称，10 月新增就业 165,000 人，失业率降至 4.1%；同期消费者价格环比涨 0.4%。成屋销售降至 2010 年以来最慢水平。

recent_coverage.title: Renewals Carry Apartment REIT Pricing as Coastal and Sun Belt Results Split
recent_coverage.summary_zh: RealPage 指出，2026 年第 3 季度续租与低流失率支撑公寓 REIT 定价，但阳光带多地新租约承压；沿海布局较重的运营商上调指引，阳光带同业下调预期。

recent_coverage.title: Legislative risk continues to cloud BTR’s capital outlook; here's why
recent_coverage.summary_zh: 尽管 BTR 获得机构投资者禁令豁免，实施规则及潜在新法仍压制资本投入。全国公寓协会数据显示，2026 年第 3 季度 BTR 在建量同比降 18.5%，社区销售额降 51.5%。

recent_coverage.title: Rising rents draw Wall Street money to industrial outdoor storage lot investments across the U.S.
recent_coverage.summary_zh: 据 Newmark 与 Alterra 数据，2020 年至今年第 3 季度，8 个主要市场工业露天堆场平均租金上涨 103.5%，每可用英亩月租近 11,000 美元，但南佛罗里达与萨凡纳涨幅落后传统工业物业。

recent_coverage.title: Building Material Price Inflation Remains High Despite Energy Price Declines
recent_coverage.summary_zh: NAHB 报告显示，10 月新建住宅投入价格环比涨 0.3%、同比涨 10.4%；能源投入价格环比降 3.3%，但建材价格仍环比涨 0.5%、同比涨 5.8%。

recent_coverage.title: SpaceX Unveils $74B Data Center Plans In Texas, Arizona
recent_coverage.summary_zh: SpaceX 宣布在亚利桑那州和得克萨斯州分别规划 500 亿和 240 亿美元数据中心项目；得州项目拟自建燃气电厂，亚利桑那项目将至少部分使用当地合作社电力。

recent_coverage.title: No Relief: Credit Conditions for Builders Still Tightening
recent_coverage.summary_zh: NAHB 调查显示，2026 年第 3 季度住宅土地收购、开发与建设贷款净宽松指数为 -15.3，连续 19 个季度收紧；各类贷款成本季度变化较小，方向不一。

recent_coverage.title: Apartment rents diverge: San Francisco rises, the Sun Belt falls
recent_coverage.summary_zh: RealPage 数据显示，10 月全国同店要价租金同比涨 1.7%，环比降 0.7%；该机构称同比改善主要来自比较基数。旧金山同比涨 14.7%，圣安东尼奥降 2.6%。

recent_coverage.title: Members Of Congress Have Questions For Brookfield After Its Mass Mobile Home Purchase
recent_coverage.summary_zh: Brookfield 第 2 季度从 GIC 收购 Yes Communities，后者运营逾 55,000 个住宅地块。3 名众议员要求其就租户保护作出保证，回复期限为 11 月 20 日。

recent_coverage.title: Compass sues 15 MLSes over listing policies
recent_coverage.summary_zh: Compass 在 8 个州分别对 15 家多重上市服务机构提起联邦反垄断诉讼，争议涉及经纪人在 MLS 之外营销部分房源可能遭罚款的挂牌规则。

recent_coverage.title: Rapid absorption continues even as deliveries slow for the Phoenix multifamily market
recent_coverage.summary_zh: Northmarq 称，2026 年第 3 季度凤凰城公寓净吸纳逾 5,500 套，交付放缓推动运营改善；稳定运营物业空置率为 6.5%，月租 1,524 美元，但销售活动放缓。

recent_coverage.title: Tucson multifamily rents push higher as vacancy tightens
recent_coverage.summary_zh: Northmarq 报告显示，2026 年第 3 季度图森公寓空置率降至 7.2%，同比下降 160 个基点；平均月租季度上涨 1.2% 至 1,163 美元，年内各季度租金均有增长。

recent_coverage.title: Raleigh-Durham multifamily vacancy tightens as deliveries slow
recent_coverage.summary_zh: Northmarq 称，2026 年第 3 季度罗利--达勒姆公寓空置率降至 7.4%；年内交付近 4,400 套，同比降 54%。月租季度降 0.4% 至 1,585 美元，同比仍涨 0.9%。

recent_coverage.title: New, pending, closed listings remain depressed in Houston
recent_coverage.summary_zh: 休斯敦地产经纪人协会数据显示，截至 11 月 9 日当周，新挂牌 3,146 套，同比降 7%；住宅签约 1,402 套，同比降 29.5%，成交 1,275 套，同比降 17%。

recent_coverage.title: MarketBeat Raleigh-Durham Life Sciences Q3 2026
recent_coverage.summary_zh: 高纬环球报告显示，2026 年第 3 季度罗利--达勒姆生命科学物业净吸纳连续第 4 个季度为正；空置率环比升至 26.4%，仍低于上年同期的 28.0%。

recent_coverage.title: CenterCal makes Arizona debut with $117M retail acquisition in tight market
recent_coverage.summary_zh: CenterCal 以 1.167 亿美元收购凤凰城郊区皮奥里亚的 Park West 购物中心，首次进入亚利桑那州。该项目占地 45 英亩，交易发生于凤凰城零售空置率下降之际。

recent_coverage.title: October 2026 Hottest Housing Markets
recent_coverage.summary_zh: Realtor.com 的 2026 年 10 月榜单显示，哈特福德居首，前 20 名连续第 37 个月仅来自东北与中西部；热门市场每套房源浏览量为全国均值的 2.6 倍。

recent_coverage.title: Oppenheimer & Co. Signs 220,000 SF Office Headquarters Lease in Lower Manhattan
recent_coverage.summary_zh: Oppenheimer 已在 RXR 持有的曼哈顿下城 32 Old Slip 签署约 220,000 平方英尺总部租约，覆盖 6 层，预计于 2028 年第 1 季度入驻。

recent_coverage.title: The seasonal decline in housing inventory is in full force
recent_coverage.summary_zh: HousingWire 数据显示，11 月 6 日至 13 日在售库存从 902,740 套降至 895,988 套，同比仍增 7.11%；该媒体指出，利率上行冲击需求，新挂牌近期变化不大。

recent_coverage.title: How Training Veterans in Skilled Trades Could Speed Up Homebuilding and Ease Housing Costs
recent_coverage.summary_zh: HBI 研究称，技工短缺使每套住宅建造时间延长近 2 个月，并导致 2024 年少建 19,000 套住宅。该机构认为，培训退伍军人及转业军人可成为补充劳动力的途径。

recent_coverage.title: Existing-Home Sales Decreased 5.5% in October, According to NAR Report
recent_coverage.summary_zh: NAR 数据显示，10 月成屋销售环比下降 5.5% 至季调年率 375 万套，同比下降 8.8%；在售库存增至 159 万套，房价中位数上涨 0.4%。

recent_coverage.title: Renters comfortably affording a house would need a $14,408 raise to buy one (October Rent Report)
recent_coverage.summary_zh: Zillow 表示，10 月全国租赁需求同比上升 22.1%，单户出租需求上升 24.3%；舒适承担单户租金的家庭仍需年收入增加 $14,408 才能购房。

recent_coverage.title: Denver multifamily rent gains broaden as construction slows
recent_coverage.summary_zh: Northmarq 称，丹佛多户市场第三季度空置率为 6.3%，平均租金环比上涨 0.7% 至每月 $1,813；交付放缓、建设管线收缩，交易活动回升。

recent_coverage.title: JLL Arranges $212.5M Sale of Senior Living Community in Lincolnwood, Illinois
recent_coverage.summary_zh: JLL 安排伊利诺伊州 Lincolnwood 一处 383 户养老社区以 $212.5M 出售并融资；SRG 与 Nuveen Real Estate 买入，贷款期限为 5 年。

recent_coverage.title: Mortgage Rates
recent_coverage.summary_zh: Freddie Mac 显示，截至 11 月 12 日，30 年期固定按揭利率为 7.11%，连续第四周下降；15 年期利率为 6.45%，两者仍高于一年前。

recent_coverage.title: Significantly Weaker Demand for Residential Mortgages and CRE Loans in Third Quarter
recent_coverage.summary_zh: NAHB 援引美联储调查称，第三季度各类住宅按揭需求显著减弱；CRE 建设开发贷款标准中度收紧，多户贷款标准温和收紧，相关需求亦显著走弱。

recent_coverage.title: Just 3 Major U.S. Metros Are Seller’s Markets–the Fewest Since the Pandemic Freeze
recent_coverage.summary_zh: Redfin 称，10 月美国人口最多的 50 个都会区中仅 3 个为卖方市场，41 个为买方市场；全国卖家数量比买家多 71%，买方议价能力处于至少 2013 年以来高位。

recent_coverage.title: Apartment Loans Fuel A Booming CRE CLO Market Not Seen Since 2021
recent_coverage.summary_zh: Bisnow 援引 Trepp 数据称，前 10 个月投资者购买 $40.2B CRE CLO 债务，同比按金额增长 66%；受利率不确定性影响，部分发行人或推迟至明年。

recent_coverage.title: JLL Brokers Sale of 330-Unit Apartment Community in Wildwood, Florida
recent_coverage.summary_zh: JLL 经纪出售佛州 Wildwood 的 330 户 The Juliette，买方为 Centennial Holding；物业建于 2024 年，成交时入住率为 96%，交易价格和贷款金额未披露。

recent_coverage.title: Broe Real Estate Group Acquires 22-Story Apartment Tower in Uptown Dallas

recent_coverage.title: More Than Half of Raleigh-Area Residents Have Considered Moving Because of Housing Costs, New Survey Finds

recent_coverage.title: Weekley Homes Spends $16M on 38-Acre Dev Site in Scottsdale

recent_coverage.title: ATTOM Reveals July as Best Month to Buy a Home Based on Lowest Premium above AVM

recent_coverage.title: GAMLS: Home prices increase despite overall market slowdown
recent_coverage.summary_zh: Georgia MLS 数据显示，亚特兰大 10 月房价中位数同比上涨 1.3% 至 $395,000；成交量同比下降 19.5%，住宅签约量同比下降 26.8%，在售库存上升 1.4%。

recent_coverage.title: Dermody Adds Tracy Warehouse to West Region Industrial Portfolio

recent_coverage.title: Monthly Mortgage Payments Fall to Lowest Level in 6 Weeks as Home Prices Keep Dipping
recent_coverage.summary_zh: Redfin 称，截至 11 月 8 日的四周，房价中位数同比下降 0.9% 至 $388,613；按 7.18% 利率计算的月度按揭支付降至 $2,755，但住宅签约量仍处记录低位。

recent_coverage.title: First Look: Construction on AT&T’s New Plano Campus Is Underway
recent_coverage.summary_zh: AT&T 已在 Plano 新总部园区铺设首条光纤并举行奠基仪式；公司预计最早于 2028 年底开始迁入员工，园区建成后可容纳 10,000 人。

recent_coverage.title: Weekly Housing Trends: U.S. Market Update (Week Ending Nov. 7, 2026)

recent_coverage.title: The Generational Housing Divide: Millennials Had It Better Than Baby Boomers–Until the Pandemic Changed the Math
recent_coverage.summary_zh: Redfin 称，疫情后按揭利率从约 3% 升至接近 7%，房价同步上涨；疫情后购房的千禧一代住房支出约占收入 35%，许多人因此被排除在市场之外。
